questions.question: The daughter cells have the same number of chromosomes when a cell divides by_________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __mitosis__.

 __Explanation-__

Mitosis-

__
 
• This is the most dramatic period of the cell cycle.
 
• Mitosis is the division of a parent cell into two identical daughter cells, each with a nucleus having the same amount of DNA, the same number and kind of chromosomes, and the same heredity as the parent cell. Therefore, it is also known as equivalent division.
 
• That is, the chromosome number in daughter cells (progeny) and mother cells (parental) becomes the same.
 
• Mitosis is divided into the following four stages-
 
 
• Prophase-
 
 
• This phase is known for the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material.
 
• In this chromatin condensation becomes untangled and finally, the centriole begins to move toward the opposite poles of the animal cell.
 
 
 
• Metaphase-
 
 
• The chromosomes spread out through the cytoplasm of the cell and seem to be the shortest and thickest.
 
 
 
• Anaphase-
 
 
• It is known to be the shortest duration phase.
 
• At the beginning of this phase, the splitting of chromosomes takes place.
 
 
 
• Telophase-
 
 
• This is considered to be a long and complex phase.
 
• In this phase, the spindle fibers disappear.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Meiosis-

 
• Meiosis is the phenomenon that occurs in any life cycle that involves the process of sexual reproduction.
 
• The production of offspring by sexual reproduction involves the fusion of two gametes.
 
• Thus, meiosis is known to be the specialized form of cell division that reduces the chromosome number in such a way that each daughter nuclei receive only one set of each kind of chromosome (i.e., maternal and paternal).

questions.question: The number of chromosomes become half in a daughter cell by the process of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell.
 
• This process is essential for sexual reproduction and occurs in the germ cells to produce gametes (sperm and eggs).
 
• Meiosis involves two sequential divisions: meiosis I and meiosis II.
 
• During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes are separated, and during meiosis II, sister chromatids are separated.
 
• The reduction in chromosome number ensures that when fertilization occurs, the resulting zygote has the correct diploid number of chromosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction commonly found in prokaryotes such as bacteria.
 
• During binary fission, the parent cell divides into two genetically identical daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis**
 
 
• Mitosis is a type of cell division that results in two daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It is involved in growth, repair, and asexual reproduction in multicellular organisms.
 
 
 
• **Amitosis**
 
 
• Amitosis is a direct method of cell division where the nucleus and cytoplasm divide without the formation of chromosomes.
 
• This process is less common and occurs in some single-celled organisms and certain tissues.

questions.question: The functions of endoplasmic reticulum are-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **All of the above**

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a critical cellular organelle involved in various functions essential for cell survival and operation. It exists in two forms: rough ER (RER) and smooth ER (SER).
 
• Rough ER has ribosomes attached to its surface, which are sites for protein synthesis.
 
• Smooth ER, on the other hand, lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.

**Explanation:**__

 
• **Mechanical Support:** The endoplasmic reticulum provides structural support to the cell by maintaining its shape and providing a scaffold that helps in the organization of the cell’s internal components.
 
• **Lipoproteins and Glycogen Production:** The smooth ER is involved in the synthesis of lipids, including phospholipids and cholesterol, which are essential for the formation of cell membranes and lipoproteins. Additionally, it plays a role in the metabolism of carbohydrates, including the conversion and storage of glycogen.
 
• **Translocation:** The rough ER is involved in the translocation of newly synthesized proteins. These proteins are either destined for secretion or for use within the cell membrane. The ER ensures that proteins are correctly folded and modified before they are transported to their final destinations.

questions.question: In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytokinesis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytokinesis** is the process during cell division where the **cytoplasm of a parental cell is divided between two daughter cells**.
 
• The formation of the **phragmoplast** occurs during cytokinesis in plant cells.
 
• The phragmoplast is a structure that serves as a **scaffold for cell plate assembly** and subsequent formation of a new cell wall separating the two daughter cells.
 
• It is essential for the successful completion of cell division in plants, ensuring that each daughter cell receives the necessary cellular components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell division** consists of two main processes: mitosis (karyokinesis) and cytokinesis.
 
• **Mitosis** is the division of the nucleus, whereas **cytokinesis** is the division of the cytoplasm.
 
• In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs through the formation of a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell into two.
 
• In plant cells, the **phragmoplast** guides the formation of a cell plate, which eventually develops into a separating cell wall.
 
• The **G0 phase** is a resting phase where the cell is not actively preparing to divide.
 
• The **S phase** is the part of the cell cycle where DNA replication occurs.

questions.question: Most centrioles have a _____ structure of triple microtubules, which are present in pairs and arranged orthogonally after duplication.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9 + 0**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Centrioles are present in pairs and are arranged orthogonally after duplication, which is essential for cell division.
 
• Each centriole is composed of nine sets of triplet microtubules arranged in a cylinder.
 
• This 9 + 0 arrangement is crucial for the formation of the centrosome and spindle fibers during mitosis and meiosis. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Centrioles play a key role in cell division, particularly in the process of mitosis and meiosis, where they help in the organization of the mitotic spindle.
 
• They are cylindrical structures that are found in most eukaryotic cells, though absent in higher plants and most fungi.
 
• The duplication of centrioles is a critical step in the cell cycle, ensuring that each daughter cell receives an appropriate number of centrioles.
 
• Abnormalities in centriole structure or number can lead to diseases, including cancer, due to errors in cell division.

questions.question: The membrane that encloses a vacuole is called.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Tonoplast.**

__**Explanation-**__

__
 
• The membrane that surrounds the vacuole of a plant cell is indeed called the tonoplast.
 
• The tonoplast is a type of cellular membrane that selectively controls the flow of molecules between the cytosol and the interior of the vacuole.
 
• This membrane plays a central role in maintaining the osmotic balance and turgor pressure of cell, which is the force exerted by water pushing the plasma membrane against the cell wall.
 
• The tonoplast also isolates harmful materials that could potentially impair the rest of the cell.
 
• The tonoplast contains a variety of proteins that are involved in transporting solutes across the membrane, as well as channels for water (aquaporins).
 
• Tonoplast aids in the regulation of ion balance, pH, and other aspects of metabolism within the cell. It's a crucial part of the cell's ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7fd79cfc662bdd3de87f4639803e8503bcd481fd67906a7be5c1efe4a9164a5.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

**Plasmalemma: **This is another term for the cell or plasma membrane. It's a biologically active boundary between the living cell and its surroundings that provides selective permeability. It's composed of a phospholipid bilayer intertwined with proteins and carbohydrates. The primary job of the plasmalemma is to regulate the exchange of materials such as ions and molecules into and out of the cell.

**Cell Membrane: **As mentioned, the cell membrane (also termed as plasma membrane or plasmalemma) is the cell's outermost line of defense against its surroundings. It controls the movement of substances in and out of cells, houses cytoplasm, and includes a variety of biological molecules, primarily lipids and proteins. This membrane helps maintain homeostasis within the cell and serves as a communication interface with other cells and the extracellular environment.

**Middle Lamella: **The middle lamella is a thin layer that is located between primary walls of plant cells. It's the first layer that forms during cell division, and it cements the cells together.The middle lamella is chiefly composed of pectic compounds, including calcium pectate and magnesium pectate. Middle lamella is not present in animal cells, it's specific to plants, algae, and some fungi.

__**Conclusion- **__The membrane that encloses a vacuole is called Tonoplast.

__
 
• The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms

• Organelles can be of two types
 
• **Membrane-bound organelle - **

questions.question: The process of cell division by which most cells in the body divide for growth is called _____.
questions.solution:
__**Concept - **__

__
 
• MITOSIS**:**

 
 
• Mitosis is a form of cell division in which one cell (the mother) divides to produce **two genetically** identical new cells (the daughters).
 
• Mitosis is the component of the cell cycle's dividing mechanism in which the DNA of the cell's nucleus is divided into two equal sets of chromosomes.
 
• Mitosis or the equational division is usually restricted to the diploid cells only.
 
• Prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase are the four basic stages of mitosis.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e7dae57e4dfad217317752b341819b6c9fb00cf442842de28bbaf5d105048385.png] 

 
• SIGNIFICANCE OF MITOSIS:
 
 
• Mitosis is involved in the vast majority of cell divisions in your body.
 
• It replaces existing, worn-out cells with new ones during an organism's existence.
 
• Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
 
• The** growth and development** of multicellular organisms are due to mitosis. Mitosis fills an organism's body with cells throughout development and growth, and it continues to do so throughout its existence.
 
• A very significant contribution to mitosis is cell repair. The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being constantly replaced.
 
 

**Explanation - **__

 
• The significance of mitosis is the cell division of cells for growth and development.

Hence the process of cell division by which most cells in the body divide for growth is called **Mitosis**.

questions.question: Mitochondria are sites of _____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Aerobic respiration.**

__**Explanation-**__

Mitochondria are often called the "**powerhouse"** of the cell since they are responsible for **aerobic cellular respiration**, a series of metabolic reactions that convert biochemical energy from nutrients into adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which can then be used by the cell for numerous processes.

**Aerobic respiration involves four key steps**: glycolysis, pyruvate decarboxylation, Krebs cycle (or citric acid cycle), and the electron transport chain.

__
 
• **Glycolysis** occurs in the cytoplasm of cells, the pyruvate produced in glycolysis is transported into the mitochondria where the rest of the processes occur. Here's a brief overview of what happens within the mitochondria:__
 
• **Pyruvate Decarboxylation: **This occurs in the matrix of the mitochondria. Each pyruvate molecule from glycolysis is decarboxylated, meaning one of its carbon atoms is removed. This carbon atom is then released as a molecule of carbon dioxide. The remaining two-carbon molecule is then oxidized, and its electrons are transferred to a molecule called Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD+) to create NADH - an energy-carrying molecule. The final product of the reaction is a molecule called Acetyl Coenzyme A (Acetyl-CoA).
 
• **Krebs Cycle (Citric Acid Cycle)**: This also occurs in the mitochondrial matrix and involves a series of chemical reactions used by all aerobic organisms to release stored energy. The Acetyl-CoA produced from Pyruvate Decarboxylation enters the cycle. Over the course of the cycle, the Acetyl-CoA is broken down and more carbon dioxide is released. The output of the Krebs Cycle for each Acetyl-CoA molecule includes 2 CO₂ molecules, 3 NADH molecules, 1 FADH₂ molecule (another type of energy-carrying molecule) and 1 ATP molecule.
 
• **Electron Transport Chain**: This happens across the inner mitochondrial membrane. The NADH and FADH₂ produced in earlier steps donate their electrons to an electron transport chain, which uses this electron flow to pump protons (H+) out of the matrix and into the intermembrane space. This creates a proton gradient.
 
• **Chemiosmosis and Oxidative Phosphorylation:** Returning to the matrix, driven by the gradient, protons pass through a protein complex called ATP synthase. The energy released by this allows ATP synthase to bind ADP to inorganic phosphate, forming ATP. At the end of the electron transport chain, electrons bind with these protons and ambient oxygen to form water.

 

In summary, the mitochondria make use of the products from glycolysis in the cytoplasm and run the reactions of pyruvate decarboxylation, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain to produce ATP, releasing carbon dioxide and water as waste products in the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

Mitochondria are small, spherical or rod-shaped organelles that are surrounded by two membranes, each a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

__
 
• **Outer Mitochondrial Membrane**: This is a porous membrane and very permeable due to protein structures called porins. It allows small molecules and ions to freely diffuse from the cytosol into the intermembrane space.
 
• **Intermembrane Space**: This is the region between the outer and inner membranes. It has an important role in the primary function of mitochondria, which is oxidative phosphorylation. The concentration of proteins here is similar to the concentration in the cytosol. It also contains enzymes that use ATP passing out of the matrix to phosphorylate other nucleotides.
 
• **Inner Mitochondrial Membrane:** This is highly impermeable to all molecules. It folds over many times to form crest-like structures called **cristae** which increases the surface area of the membrane and therefore its ability to produce ATP. This membrane also has transport proteins that move proteins from the intermembrane space into the matrix. The electron transport chain and ATP synthase are located in the inner membrane.
 
• **Matrix: **This is the space enclosed by the inner membrane. It contains dozens of enzymes, including those required for the oxidation of pyruvate and fatty acids, and for the citric acid cycle (also known as the Krebs cycle or TCA). The mitochondrial DNA, ribosomes, and additional enzymes necessary for the expression of this DNA are all found within the matrix.

Mitochondria are unique because they have their own DNA, distinct from the nuclear DNA of the cell.

**Conclusion- **__ Mitochondria are sites of aerobic respiration.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is called the Master of the Cell?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A nucleus is a membrane-enclosed organelle within a cell and regulates the functionalities of a cell like metabolism, hereditary etc.**
 
• **It is also called the central unit or master of the cell because it contains chromosomes that carry genetic information. Hence option 4 is correct.**
 
• The nucleus contains a nuclear membrane that surrounds the external part of the nucleus which is called the nuclear envelope.
 
• The pores present on the nuclear membrane allow certain molecules like proteins and nucleic acids to pass through it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Mitochondria or a powerhouse of a cell** is a membrane-bound organelle present in the cytoplasm of all eukaryotic cells (cells with defined nuclei).

• **The endoplasmic reticulum is a large structure that regulates calcium storage, protein synthesis and lipid metabolism in the cell.**

questions.question: In 1838 __________ and ___________ formulated the “cell theory.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** M.J. Schleiden, Theodore Schwann **

__**Explanation**__**:**

__
 
• In 1838, Matthias Jakob Schleiden, a German botanist, and Theodor Schwann, a German physiologist, independently formulated the cell theory.
 
• Schleiden proposed that all plants are composed of cells, while Schwann extended this idea to animals, stating that all living organisms are made up of cells.
 
• Their combined work laid the foundation for the modern cell theory, which states that:-

 
• All living organisms are composed of one or more cells.
 
• The cell is the basic unit of structure and organization in organisms.
 
• All cells come from pre-existing cells through cell division.

**Conclusion**__**:-**In 1838, M.J. Schleiden and Theodore Schwann formulated the “cell theory.”

questions.question: In which of the following cell organelles does DNA replication take place in eukaryotic cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus**__**__.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• DNA replication is the process by another copy of the DNA molecule is made within the cell.
 
• This process is vital for cell division process.
 
• In **eukaryotic cells**, the **DNA is present inside the membrane-bound nucleus**.
 
• Thus, the **replication** process also takes place inside the **nucleus**.
 
• However, in **prokaryotic** cells, the DNA is present a region of the cytoplasm, and hence, its replication also occurs in **cytoplasm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Ribosome: **

 
 
• A ribosome is an intercellular structure made of both **RNA and protein.**
 
• It is the site of protein synthesis in the cell. 
 
 
 
• **Lysosome:**
 
 
• A lysosome is a **membrane-bound **cell organelle that contains digestive enzymes.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm**:
 
 
• It is the gelatinous liquid that fills the inside of a cell.
 
• It is composed of water, salts, and various organic molecules. 
 
• Some intracellular organelles, such the nucleus and mitochondria, are enclosed by membranes that separate them from the cytoplasm.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:** 
 
 
• A nucleus, as related to **genomics**, is the membrane-enclosed organelle within a cell that contains the chromosomes.

questions.question: Which of the following is surrounded by single-membrane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Lysosome**.

__**Explanation-**__

__
 
• **Lysosomes**__: Lysosomes are **single-membrane** structures found in the cells of animals.
 
• They are mainly involved in the digestion of macromolecules and waste disposal.
 
• They contain a wide variety of enzymes (approximately 50 different types) that can break down all types of biological polymers—proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.
 
• These enzymes function optimally at an acidic pH, which is maintained inside the lysosome.
 
• The single membrane surrounding the lysosome serves to isolate these potent enzymes from the rest of the cell, preventing enzymatic digestion of the cell's own components.

 

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Mitochondria__ are also double-membrane organelles, found in almost all eukaryotic cells.
 
• They are known as the "powerhouses" of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• The outer membrane of the mitochondria is quite porous and allows the passage of ions and small proteins, while the inner membrane is impermeable to most substances.
 
• The inner portion of the mitochondria, called the matrix, is where the citric acid cycle (also known as Krebs cycle or TCA cycle) takes place. The inner membrane shows numerous infoldings, called cristae, which enhance the surface area for oxidative phosphorylation, the main process by which ATP is produced.

** **

__
 
• **Nucleus__:** The nucleus of a cell is surrounded by the nuclear envelope or nuclear membrane. This nuclear membrane is a **double-membrane structure**, meaning it has two layers, an outer membrane, and an inner membrane.
 
• Outer Nuclear Membrane: This is continuous with the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), a network of membranous tubules in the cytoplasm. The outer nuclear membrane is covered in ribosomes, just like the endoplasmic reticulum, and it's involved in protein synthesis and lipid metabolism.
 
• Inner Nuclear Membrane: This membrane separates the nucleus, including the nucleolus and other nuclear bodies, from the cytoplasm. The inner nuclear membrane contains proteins that anchor the nuclear lamina, a mesh-like network of protein filaments that provide mechanical support to the nucleus and also regulate important cellular events such as DNA replication and cell division.
 
• Between the outer and inner nuclear membranes is the perinuclear space, which is continuous with the space inside the endoplasmic reticulum

 

__
 
• **Chloroplast**:__ These are **double-membrane** organelles found in plant cells and are responsible for photosynthesis, the process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• The outer membrane of the chloroplast is smooth and allows small molecules and proteins to pass to the intermembrane space. The inner membrane is less permeable and has transport proteins embedded in it.
 
• Inside the inner membrane is the stroma, a fluid-filled space that contains the DNA, ribosomes, and enzymes required for photosynthesis.
 
• Most importantly, the stroma contains multiple flattened sacs called thylakoids, which are organized into stacks called grana. The thylakoids contain the photosynthetic pigments (chlorophyll) where light absorption for photosynthesis occurs.

__**Conclusion- **__ Lysosome is single membranous in nature.

questions.question: Regarding Meiosis, which of the statements is incorrect?

options.text: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of Meiosis-II
There are two stages in Meiosis, Meiosis-I and II
DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination occurs in Meiosis-I

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3**.

**Solution**

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The eukaryotic **cell cycle** is divided into two phases: the **Interphase and the M phase**.
 
• M phase or **mitosis** is the phase where actual **cell division** occurs.
 
• **Interphase** is the phase between **two successive mitosis divisions**.

**Explanation:**__

Interphase is divided into three phases; **G₁ phase, S phase, and G₂ phase**.

__
 
• **G₁ Phase**

 
 
• It is the **time period between mitosis and the beginning of DNA replication**.
 
• **DNA does not replicate** in this phase.
 
 
 
• **S phase**
 
 
• It is also known as the **Synthesis phase**.
 
• **DNA replication occurs **in this phase.
 
• Here the **number of DNA** molecules increases by **double fold**.
 
 
 
• **G₂ Phase**
 
 
• In this phase **protein synthesis** occurs.
 
 
 
• Prior to meiosis, the cell goes through an **interphase** period during which it** replicates its chromosomes and checks all of its systems to ensure that it is ready to divide**.
 
• Interphase is a stage before meiosis and hence not a part of **meiosis.**

So, the **correct answer is option 3.**

**Additional Information:**__

 
• The cell division which results in the **production of a haploid set of chromosomes** is called **Meiosis.**
 
• There are two stages in Meiosis; **Meiosis I and Meiosis II**.
 
• The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis and is generally short-lived.
 
• There is no replication of DNA during interkinesis. Interkinesis is followed by prophase II, a much simpler prophase than prophase I. 
 
• At the end of **Meiosis II**, **four haploid cells** are formed.

questions.question: Which one of the following does not exist in the nucleus of a cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastids**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Plastids are **organelles found in the cells of plants and algae, **not in the nucleus.
 
• They are responsible for **photosynthesis, storage of products like starch, **and the **synthesis of many classes of molecules** such as fatty acids and terpenes which are necessary for the cell.
 
• Plastids** share a similar origin, **deriving from endosymbiotic cyanobacteria.
 
• They **contain their own DNA**, which is distinct from the nuclear DNA of the cell.
 
• **Types of plastids include chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and leucoplasts, **each with specialized functions.
 
• Chloroplasts, in particular, are involved in photosynthesis and contain the pigment chlorophyll.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chromatin fibres are a complex of DNA and protein found in the nucleus, which condenses to form chromosomes during cell division.
